items.text: What is the standard scale for residential floor plans and elevations?
B. One-quarter inch equals one foot — Floor plans and elevations use the 1/4 inch = 1 foot (1:48) architect's scale; 1 inch = 20 feet is the engineer's site-plan scale.
On a floor plan drawn at one-quarter inch equals one foot, a wall measures 6 inches on paper. How long is the actual wall?
C. 24 feet — At 1/4 inch = 1 foot, plan inches times 4 gives feet, so 6 inches on paper = 24 feet actual.
What kind of scale is normally used for a site or plot plan?

A. An engineer's decimal scale, such as one inch equals twenty feet — Site and plot plans use the engineer's decimal scale (1 inch = 20 or 30 feet), while the architect's scale is fractional (1/4 inch = 1 foot).
Which drawing shows what is INSIDE the wall assembly - framing, insulation, and floor-to-floor heights?
D. Section — A section is a vertical slice through the building showing the assembly interior; an elevation shows only the flat exterior or interior face.
On a plan, a detail bubble reads 3 over A5. What does that mean?
A. Detail number 3 found on sheet A5 — The detail reference reads detail number over sheet number, so 3/A5 means detail 3 on sheet A5.
What size is a door with the schedule callout 2868?
B. 2 feet 8 inches wide by 6 feet 8 inches high — In schedule callouts the first pair is width in feet-inches and the second is height, so 2868 = 2 feet 8 inches by 6 feet 8 inches.
The window symbol on the plan disagrees with the size listed on the window schedule. Which controls?
C. The schedule controls the size — The schedule, not the plan symbol, controls the window or door size.
On a floor plan, what does a hidden (dashed) line typically represent?

D. An object above or below the cut plane, such as upper cabinets, a roof overhang, or a footing — A hidden or dashed line shows an object above or below the cut plane, like upper cabinets, a roof overhang, or a footing under a wall.
The drawings show one flashing detail but the written specifications require a different product. What should the builder do?

A. Follow the specs, which generally govern quality - and notify the architect for clarification before proceeding — Specs govern quality and generally govern in a conflict, but the standard exam answer is to notify the architect or designer for clarification before proceeding.
A dimension string reads 12 feet 6 inches, but scaling the drawing gives about 12 feet 9 inches. Which do you use?
B. The written dimension - never scale a drawing when a figure is given — Written dimensions always beat scaled dimensions; never scale a drawing when a figure is given.
In the classic 16-division CSI MasterFormat, which division covers concrete?
C. Division 3 — CSI Division 3 is Concrete; Division 4 is Masonry, Division 2 is Sitework, and Division 6 is Wood and Plastics.
How many board feet are in one 2x6 that is 10 feet long?
D. 10 board feet — BF = (thickness x width x length in feet) / 12, so 2 x 6 x 10 / 12 = 10 board feet.
What does 800 board feet of lumber cost at 600 dollars per thousand board feet?
A footing runs 100 lineal feet, 16 inches wide and 8 inches thick. How much concrete is that before waste?
C. About 3.3 cubic yards — 100 x 1.333 x 0.667 = 88.9 cubic feet, divided by 27 = about 3.3 cubic yards.
A block wall is 40 feet long and 8 feet high. Using the standard count for 8 by 8 by 16 CMU, how many blocks are needed before waste?
B. 360 blocks — Standard 8x8x16 CMU runs 1.125 blocks per square foot: 40 x 8 = 320 sq ft x 1.125 = 360 blocks.
A roof measures 2,400 square feet. How many bundles of standard three-tab shingles are needed before waste?
D. 72 bundles — One square = 100 sq ft, so 2,400 sq ft = 24 squares, and at 3 bundles per square that is 72 bundles (add about 10 percent waste).
A 12 by 16 foot room has an 8-foot ceiling. Before openings and waste, how many 4x8 drywall sheets cover the walls and ceiling?
B. 20 sheets — Walls: 56-foot perimeter x 8 = 448 sq ft; ceiling 192 sq ft; total 640 / 32 sq ft per sheet = 20 sheets.
Using the takeoff formula for studs at 16 inches on center, how many studs does a 40-foot wall need before corner and opening extras?
A. 31 studs — Studs at 16 inches on center = (length x 0.75) + 1, so 40 x 0.75 + 1 = 31 studs, before adding for corners, intersections, and openings.
How many floor joists at 16 inches on center are needed along a 24-foot run?
C. 19 joists — (24 x 0.75) + 1 = 19 joists.
You need 100 compacted cubic yards of fill with 10 percent shrinkage. About how much bank material must be excavated?
D. About 111 bank cubic yards — Compacted fill shrinks below bank volume, so divide: 100 / 0.90 = about 111 bank cubic yards.
A basement dig measures 40 feet by 30 feet by 6 feet deep. How many bank cubic yards is that?
A. 267 bank cubic yards — 40 x 30 x 6 = 7,200 cubic feet / 27 = 267 bank cubic yards; 333 is the loose volume after 25 percent swell, a trap.
What ground slope away from the foundation does MRC R401.3 require?

B. 6 inches of fall in the first 10 feet (a 5 percent grade) — R401.3 requires 6 inches of fall in the first 10 feet away from the foundation, a 5 percent grade; impervious surfaces need a minimum 2 percent.
A slope of one-quarter inch per foot equals approximately what percent grade?
A. About 2 percent — 0.25 / 12 = 2.08 percent, about 2 percent - the standard sewer and flatwork slope; one-eighth inch per foot is about 1 percent.
A gable end is 24 feet wide with a 6-foot rise. What is its area?
C. 72 square feet — Triangle area = base x height / 2, so 24 x 6 / 2 = 72 square feet.
What are Michigan's maximum stair riser and minimum tread depth?

C. Eight and one-quarter inch riser, nine inch tread — Michigan amendments allow a maximum 8-1/4 inch riser and minimum 9-inch tread; the IRC's 7-3/4 and 10 are trap answers, and maximum variance is 3/8 inch.
Which law currently governs plumbing, electrical, AND mechanical licensing in Michigan?

D. The Skilled Trades Regulation Act, PA 407 of 2016 — The Skilled Trades Regulation Act (PA 407 of 2016, MCL 339.5101-339.6133) repealed and replaced the old trade acts, whose names are trap answers on current-law questions.
How many hours of experience does a journeyman plumber license require in Michigan?

B. 6,000 hours over 3 years — Under the STRA, a journeyman plumber needs 6,000 hours over 3 years (a master needs 4,000 more); 8,000 and 12,000 hours are the electrician journeyman and master numbers.
A building permit expires when work has not started, or has been suspended or abandoned, for how long?
C. 180 days — MRC R105.5 sets permit expiration at 180 days without starting work or with work suspended or abandoned.
Below what calculated floor area are sealed (architect- or engineer-stamped) plans NOT required for a one- or two-family dwelling?
A. 3,500 square feet — Under Act 230, one- and two-family dwellings under 3,500 square feet of calculated floor area do not require sealed plans.
Under MRC R105.2, which retaining wall is exempt from a building permit?

D. A wall not over 4 feet from the bottom of the footing to the top, not supporting a surcharge — R105.2 exempts retaining walls not over 4 feet measured from the bottom of the footing to the top and not supporting a surcharge; 7 feet is the fence exemption.
